question: Why do young women in cities struggle to find work?

brief.question: Why do young women in cities struggle to find work?
brief.answer: Young women in urban areas have markedly lower labour force participation and higher unemployment than their rural peers. In 2025, the LFPR for urban women aged 15-29 was 23.2 % versus 29.3 % in rural areas (‑6.1 pp), while the unemployment rate was 18.9 % in urban areas compared with 8.6 % in rural areas (+10.3 pp).

findings.task: Compare labour force participation rate (LFPR) for young women (age 15-29) in urban areas vs rural areas, 2025, usual status, All India. Provide the percentage points difference.
findings.summary: In 2025, urban young women (age 15-29) had an LFPR of 23.2 %, while rural young women had 29.3 %, a difference of -6.1 percentage points.
findings.reason: Urban young women’s LFPR is 23.2% and rural is 29.3%, giving an urban‑minus‑rural gap of -6.1 percentage points.

findings.task: Compare unemployment rate (UR) for young women (age 15-29) in urban areas vs rural areas, 2025, usual status, All India. Provide the percentage points difference.
findings.summary: In 2025, the unemployment rate for urban young women was 18.9% and for rural young women 8.6%, a difference of 10.3 percentage points higher in urban areas.

PROFILE labour force participation rate (LFPR), annual, 2025, usual status (PS+SS), ages 15+ unless stated

  - The gap urban minus rural (-10.6 points overall) varies across state: from -23.5 (Sikkim) to +2.2 (Goa); set apart as outliers (possibly small, noisy samples): Chandigarh +56.1
strongest correlations across states:
  - LFPR female and LFPR male: r = 0.41 over 36 states
  - LFPR urban and LFPR rural: r = 0.38 over 36 states -- rank correlation 0.67 disagrees; driven by Chandigarh
  - LFPR and UR: r = -0.15 over 36 states
biggest changes since last release:
